text: A ___ bifurcation occurs when two fixed points (one stable, one an unstable saddle) collide and annihilate as a parameter changes, and is the mechanism underlying bistability with two stable states separated by an unstable saddle.
explanation: A saddle-node bifurcation is exactly this collision-and-annihilation event between a stable and an unstable (saddle) fixed point; before the collision, the system can be bistable with two stable states separated by the saddle, a common model for irreversible cell-fate commitment. This is distinct from a Hopf bifurcation (which creates oscillations, not bistability) or a pitchfork bifurcation (which requires a symmetric system splitting one stable point into two).
